key_concepts: Magnets attract objects made of iron, cobalt, and nickel
Magnets do not attract all metals
Common magnet shapes include ring, rectangular, horseshoe, and bar magnets
Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole
Cutting a magnet produces two magnets, each with a north and south pole
Magnetic force is the push or pull exerted by magnets
Like magnetic poles repel; unlike magnetic poles attract
Magnetic force is strongest at the poles and weaker in the middle
A magnetic field is the area around a magnet where magnetic force acts
Magnetic field strength decreases with distance from the magnet
Magnetic force can act through some non-magnetic materials such as plastic, wood, and pape
Iron can block or cut magnetic force
